title: 2021 Fall AMC 12B Problem 18
statement: Set \(u_0 = \dfrac{1}{4},\) and for \(k \ge 0\) let \(u_{k+1}\) be determined by the recurrence \[u_{k+1} = 2u_k - 2u_k^2.\] This sequence tends to a limit; call it \(L.\) What is the least value of \(k\) such that \[|u_k - L| \le \dfrac{1}{2^{1000}}?\]

solutions.text:
The limit satisfies \(L = 2L - 2L^2,\) giving \(L = \tfrac12.\) Let \(v_k = 1 - 2u_k.\) Then \[ \begin{aligned} v_{k+1} &= 1 - 2u_{k+1} \\ &= 1 - 4u_k + 4u_k^2 \\ &= (1 - 2u_k)^2 = v_k^2. \end{aligned} \]

Since \(v_0 = 1 - 2 \cdot \tfrac14 = \tfrac12,\) we get \(v_k = \left(\tfrac12\right)^{2^k},\) so \(|u_k - L| = \dfrac{|v_k|}{2} = 2^{-2^k - 1}.\)

We need \(2^k + 1 \ge 1000,\) i.e. \(2^k \ge 999.\) The least such \(k\) is \(10,\) since \(2^{10} = 1024.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The substitution gives \(v_{k+1} = v_k^2,\) so \(v_k\) squares repeatedly
